newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues rules on certificates of credit.
newsitem.headline: China issues rules on certificates of credit.

text.p: China's central bank has issued rules governing domestic companies using certificates of credit for settlement, banning unauthorised banks from issuing them, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.

The People's Bank of China, the central bank, said domestic firms could settle their accounts using certificates issued by designated banks to help promote China's internal trade and the development of a market economy, the newspaper said.
Under the rules, effective from August 1, only banks appointed by the central bank as well as approved bank branches could issue the certificates for settling domestic trading accounts, it said.

"Unapproved banking institutions, urban and rural credit offices and all non-banking financial institutions may not issue certificates of credit or settle domestic trading accounts using the certificates," the newspaper said.
The certificates could only be used to settle accounts among domestic firms and must not be used to retrieve cash, it said.
Such certificates were nothing more than commercial paper for settlement among domestic companies, and had no connection with agreements regarding goods and services among firms, the newspaper said.
